page.layout: One page of text, one column. Above the text: page number at head, a typographic ornament, then a centred title in capitals with a subtitle in small capitals and roman. Running text in one column with a large woodcut-style initial at the start, the verses set in italic with line breaks, and two centred small-capitals headings ("In eundem.") between the poems. Ends with a signature-like word "Hac" at lower right, which is a catchword-like word at the foot of the text. No margin notes.

l.i: XIstus aquam pauper Caprarius
ante bibebat,
Nunc summus præsul Cretica vina
bibit. Mutata quod forte licet: námque optima semper
Romæ Pontifices vina bibere pij.
At illum pudeat dices, quod plura bibaci
Dum tractat genium pocula siccat anu:
Quod crudum celsa resupinus sede meracum
Ructat, quod Gallos potus ad arma vocat:
Hoc pariter liceat. Nam potus si furit ille,
Quid summo indignum Præsule,
quæso, facit?
Ebrius in Gallum torques tua fulmina regem
Terribilesque rotas Xiste superbe minas.
Frustra: nam vino cur sobrius ille timeret
Vuida vasani fulmina Pontificis?
Quum Xistus semper sit potus, non tamen ille
Vera unquam dicit, sed fera multa facit.
Aut bibit, aut nummos propria componit in arca, A-
ut amens Xistus fulmina saua rotat.

page.notes: The page number 120 is printed at top left. The title and subtitle are set in capitals and small capitals. The woodcut initial X is read as "X" joined to "ISTVS". Some verses have doubtful readings: "Vuida vasani" and "saua" may be misprints for "Vuida vasani" (as printed) and "sæva"; "Frustra:nam" is printed with a colon after Frustra. The word "Hac" at the foot is a closing word, shown both as catchword and as a paragraph; the sign of closing is ambiguous. Words in italic are rendered with <i>; long s has been normalised to s. Line-by-line verse is set in one paragraph per stanza as required.
